name: Canberra Times cryptic crossword, Sunday 6 November 1983

clue.text: This acid puts Ann in a spasm

indicators.note: 'puts Ann in' places the name inside the other word, which wraps around it

blocks.note: a tic is an involuntary muscular twitch
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some chemical makes poor Ann twitch uncontrollably.
explanation.definitionFit: Tannic acid is the astringent compound found in tea, oak bark and wine, so the word names an acid.

clue.text: Before noon I go to see a friend from Madrid

blocks.note: a.m. means before midday
taken as written

explanation.surface: I set off one morning to visit a Spanish pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for friend, so a friend from Madrid.

clue.text: I've come under an upset, making me unsophisticated

indicators.note: in a down clue an upset word is turned over, so it reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the little word an, turned over
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Coming in under someone's upset leaves me looking green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come under' places I'VE below the reversed AN in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means innocent and lacking worldly experience, a synonym of unsophisticated.

clue.text: Incinerated by articles of faith about floor covering

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the faith word wraps the covering

blocks.note: a creed is a statement of religious belief
a mat lies on the floor

explanation.surface: Something was burned up by zealots over a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: Cremated means burned to ashes, used of a body, so it matches incinerated.

clue.text: Give out when time's up

indicators.note: in a down entry 'up' sends the letters climbing, so they read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Collapse once your hour has come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time's up' sounds like the end; in a down clue 'up' reverses the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to send out light, heat or sound, so to give it out.

clue.text: Cavity wherein you may see insect with spirit

blocks.note: an ant is an insect
rum is a distilled spirit

explanation.surface: A hollow where a bug sits beside some liquor.
explanation.definitionFit: An antrum is an anatomical cavity, such as a sinus within a bone.

clue.text: Unions can easily be in complete accord

indicators.note: saying letters can easily be something else invites forming a new word from them

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Trade unions may well agree completely.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the noun in the phrase 'in unison', which 'in complete accord' mirrors.
explanation.definitionFit: Unison is simultaneous agreement in action or voice, i.e. complete accord.

clue.text: Cow gets 6's last in its first

blocks.note: the last part of 6 down, ANTRUM
taken as written
the first part of 6 down, ANTRUM

explanation.surface: A cow is fed the end of something and then its beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a placement signal, but it simply supplies its own two letters between the two halves of the cavity word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow chews the cud, so it is an example of a ruminant animal.

clue.text: It's heavenly to take a meal about six

indicators.note: 'about' means around, so the meal word goes around the number

blocks.note: to dine is to eat a meal
Roman numeral for six

explanation.surface: Eating at around six o'clock is bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: Divine describes what belongs to God or heaven, a direct synonym of heavenly.

clue.text: Driver who is most cut up by unruly riot

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters following are thrown out of order
a word cut up by another is split open with the other placed inside its gap

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A driver is badly hurt in a rowdy disturbance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up' reads as upset or injured, but it tells you MOST is split by the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorist is someone who drives a car, so a driver.

clue.text: One war's enough to upset the girl

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A single war is enough to distress the young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Old-style clueing: 'the girl' stands for any girl's name, here the one in Scott's Ivanhoe.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowena is a female given name, so it is an example of a girl in crossword shorthand.

clue.text: Animal returns with strong mooing sound

indicators.note: something that returns comes back the way it went, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud or strong
cattle low, the old word for mooing

explanation.surface: A beast comes back to the herd with a loud moo.
explanation.walkthrough: F (musical forte) plus LOW gives FLOW, which read backwards is WOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: The wolf is a wild carnivorous mammal of the dog family, an example of an animal.

clue.text: The use of white gum entirely hides kind of skin

indicators.note: the earlier words hide something tucked inside their run of letters

blocks.clueFragment: The use of white gum entirely
blocks.note: found running across whiTE GUM ENTirely

explanation.surface: Applying white gum all over conceals a type of skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tegument is a natural covering or integument of an animal or plant, a type of skin.

clue.text: Sun might confuse weapon maker

indicators.note: to confuse is to muddle, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Glare from the sun might bewilder someone who forges arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunsmith makes and repairs firearms, a specific kind of weapon maker.

clue.text: Cure needed for this off-white colour?

indicators.note: the letters are needed to build this, signalling that they are reworked into it

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A remedy is wanted for a pale shade, as if the colour were sick.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the loose cluing: the colour is 'off', and the word for it is built from the letters of the remedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is the pale greyish-yellow of unbleached linen, an off-white shade.

clue.text: Fond of an intermittent arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things into a new order, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone likes a schedule that comes and goes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intermittent arrangement' reads as one phrase, but the definition is the single adjective and 'arrangement' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens off and on stops and starts at intervals, which is intermittent.

clue.text: Showy insect around burnt residue

indicators.note: 'around' tells you the first word encloses what follows

blocks.note: a fly is an insect
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A brightly coloured bug buzzes over the embers.
explanation.definitionFit: Flashy means ostentatiously smart or gaudy, a synonym of showy.

clue.text: Aim highly, for praise maybe

indicators.note: maybe hints the letters could be something other than what is shown, so rearrange them

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Set lofty goals, perhaps to win acclaim.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to have ambitions towards something lofty, to aim high.

clue.text: A stitch to make us true

indicators.note: to make something from the given letters is to construct a new word out of them

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A single stitch of needlework will keep us honest.
explanation.definitionFit: A suture is a surgical stitch closing a wound, so the noun matches a stitch.

clue.text: Indian emblem for bet ting agency with 1000

blocks.note: the tote is the totalisator, the official betting agency, called the TAB in Australia
Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: A symbol of a tribe stands in for a bookmaker holding a grand.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan splits 'betting' across a line break as 'bet ting'.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is a natural object or animal adopted as the emblem of a clan, notably among North American Indian peoples.

clue.text: Gathering in 23?

blocks.note: surface reading: an assembly of people
setter's reading: gathered fabric, a pleated frill made of the material at 23 down

explanation.walkthrough: 23 down is lace; 'gathering' means a meeting until the sewing sense of gathered fabric is seen.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a frill of gathered lace or fabric used to trim garments.

clue.text: Grass seen as father splits plum

indicators.note: to split something is to break it open, so the other letters sit in the gap

blocks.note: taken as written
'as' taken as written, with 'seen' as a joining word
pa is a familiar word for dad

explanation.surface: Dad cleaves a plum, and the result looks like grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seen' only joins, leaving the little word to be inserted. Paspalum is a pasture grass familiar in Australia, where this puzzle ran.
explanation.definitionFit: Paspalum is a genus of pasture grasses, common in Australia, so it names a grass.

clue.text: Material to fasten your shoe?

blocks.note: first meaning: a delicate open-work fabric
second meaning: to tie up a shoe with its cord

explanation.walkthrough: One word is both a fabric and the verb for tying up footwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Lace is an open-work fabric, and to lace a shoe is to fasten it with its laces.

clue.text: Untouched in diplomacy

blocks.note: taken as written
tact is skill in handling people delicately

explanation.walkthrough: 'In diplomacy' reads as a phrase about being diplomatic; split it into IN plus a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Intact means whole and undamaged, left exactly as it was, i.e. untouched.

clue.text: Quicker way to get an abbreviated tonsure

blocks.note: something abbreviated is made brief
absorbed into the phrase, giving no letters
a tonsure is a haircut, the shaven crown of a monk

explanation.surface: A monk wants a speedy route to a trimmed tonsure.
explanation.walkthrough: A short cut is literally an abbreviated haircut; the phrase doubles as a quicker route.
explanation.definitionFit: A shortcut is a more direct route or method that saves time, a quicker way.

clue.text: Basket containing hot meat for each

blocks.note: ham is a cured meat, here hot (cooked) meat
per means for each, as in a price per head

explanation.surface: A picnic basket packed with warm meat for everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: The parse is loose: 'hot' may hint at H starting the answer, but HAM plus PER already gives every letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A hamper is a large lidded wicker basket, often packed with food.
